description: The image displays two side-by-side bar charts illustrating the relationship between Fleiss Kappa (a measure of inter-rater reliability) and two different ambiguity metrics: “Ambiguity Std” on the left and “Max Ambiguity” on the right. Both charts share the same vertical axis, labeled “Fleiss Kappa,” ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, with values explicitly labeled above each bar. In the left chart, “Ambiguity Std” is plotted along the horizontal axis with four categories: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94. The corresponding Fleiss Kappa values are 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24, respectively, with bar heights decreasing then slightly increasing, and bar colors transitioning from dark blue to light blue as ambiguity increases. In the right chart, “Max Ambiguity” is plotted with three integer categories: 1, 2, and 3. The corresponding Fleiss Kappa values are 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, showing a clear decreasing trend as maximum ambiguity increases, with the same dark-to-light blue color gradient. Both charts visually suggest that higher ambiguity correlates with lower agreement among raters, as measured by Fleiss Kappa, consistent with the paper’s focus on evaluating human judgment reliability in the context of social engineering attacks and LLM-generated content.
